references.text: The same chapter elaborates on how the Israelites are to treat the poor among them, by opening their hand and lending to them.
It acknowledges that the poor will always be in the land, balancing the promise in verse 4 with a realistic expectation.
The Lord's blessing over the land and all work is tied to obedience to His commands.
A command to help a poor brother, referencing how the Lord brought them out of Egypt and gave them the land of Canaan.
The promise of rest and an inheritance in the land that the Lord gives, linked to God's blessing.
Blessing over all work is tied to care for Levites, foreigners, fatherless children, and widows.
In the first Christian community, there were no needy among them, as a fulfillment of the ideal from Deuteronomy.
A messianic psalm that speaks of the king delivering the poor and the one in distress.
The promise of the Lord's blessing when one feeds the hungry and satisfies the suffering.
